event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: DPZ’s 2024 filing frames COVID-19 as an event that produced tangible operational disruptions between 2020 and 2023 and that still presents a meaningful, though moderating, threat.  The company describes concrete historical impacts—labour shortages, elevated turnover, supply-chain interruptions and delayed store openings—while also warning that macro-demand, consumer behaviour, and growth trajectories remain unpredictable as the pandemic’s after-effects unwind.  These are largely factual, backward-looking statements coupled with forward-looking cautions; they reference real operating changes already taken, but do not quantify hard dollar amounts.  Because the event is now four years old, the Time Decay Principle places the evidence in the “medium-term” bucket; scores therefore sit in the 4-6 range depending on the immediacy and severity of each disclosure.  Overall, the language is specific to COVID-19, acknowledges material adverse possibilities and cites direct operational consequences, warranting a moderate risk assessment rather than either a negligible or extreme one.

evidence_list.snippet: We and our franchisees have faced an increasingly competitive labor market in recent years due to labor shortages and increased turnover at times resulting in part from the COVID-19 pandemic which caused us and our franchisees to in certain cases make operational changes and delay store openings which could ultimately impact our growth and competitive position.

components.reason: Directly links labor shortages and higher turnover to COVID-19.
Describes concrete operational impacts (operational changes, delayed store openings).
Highlights potential strategic downside (growth and competitive position).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides a specific causal chain from the pandemic to labour shortages and delayed expansion, signalling a moderate-high medium-term risk (6/10).

evidence_list.snippet: While the Company saw an increase in sales in certain markets, including within the U.S., at times during the COVID-19 pandemic, including higher sales related to heightened reliance on delivery and carryout businesses, future sales are not possible to estimate, and it is unclear what sales will be as consumer behavior and general economic and business activity move on from the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Acknowledges pandemic-driven demand volatility and forecasting uncertainty.
Explicitly ties uncertainty to future consumer behaviour post-COVID-19.
Notes prior sales uptick (a mitigating element).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Balanced by a mitigating prior sales uplift, but still flags material forecasting risk; lands at the lower end of medium severity (3/10).

evidence_list.snippet: Health epidemics or pandemics – such as the global outbreak of COVID-19 in early 2020 – have in the past and may in the future impact macroeconomic conditions, consumer behavior, labor availability and supply chain management, as well as local operations in impacted markets.

components.reason: Lists multiple critical business dimensions potentially affected by COVID-19.
Forward-looking statement of continuing exposure (‘may in the future’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but comprehensive statement of continuing pandemic risk across key value-drivers; merits a solid mid-range score (4/10).

evidence_list.snippet: While there historically has been some level of ordinary course turnover of employees, the COVID-19 pandemic and its effects exacerbated labor shortages and increased turnover in recent years.

components.reason: States that COVID-19 directly worsened labour shortages and turnover.
Positions the effect as recent and ongoing (‘in recent years’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights a sustained HR impact attributed to COVID-19, elevating operational risk to mid-level severity (5/10).

evidence_list.snippet: We have in the past experienced disruptions within our supply chain resulting from, among other things, capacity, volume, systems, staffing, operational and COVID-19-related challenges and may experience such supply chain disruptions again in the future, which could materially and adversely affect our business and operational results.

components.reason: Cites actual historical supply-chain disruptions linked to COVID-19.
Warns of repeat disruptions with ‘materially and adversely’ severe phrasing.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines past evidence with explicit warning of future material impact, supporting a firm medium-level risk score (5/10).
